has_cached_picture.description:
HasCachedPicture is true when the API has a server-side GCS copy
of the profile picture that the dashboard can purge with DELETE
/channels/:id/whatsapp/profile/picture. Not part of the Meta
response — populated by the handler from channel config — so it
is omitted on the outbound Meta calls (no `omitempty` issue).

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description: Last30d is the observation window the projection is built on.

by_operation_usd.description:
ByOperation breaks the spend down, because "IA: R$43" invites the
question "doing what?".

cached_tokens.description:
CachedTokens and InputTokens make the prompt-caching saving visible
(K3): the ratio between them is how well the prompt is layered, and
without it "structured for caching" is an unverifiable claim.

rate_cents.description:
RateCents is the USD→BRL rate applied, exposed so the number can be
checked rather than trusted.

total_brl_cents.description:
TotalBRLCents is TotalUSD converted at the platform rate, rounded
ONCE at the end. Rounding each entry first would drift by cents on a
busy account — and cents are the entire credibility of a
"no markup" line.

total_usd.description: TotalUSD is the raw provider cost.

handoff_pct.description: conversations where a human took over

account_name.description: AccountName is joined on listing reads; empty elsewhere.

is_negative.description:
IsNegative is derived (net < 0), surfaced for the owner panel's
recurring-negative-margin flag. Never stored.

business_hours_days.description:
BusinessHoursDays is a bitmask of weekdays when the bot responds:
bit 0 = Sunday, ..., bit 6 = Saturday. 0 means 24/7 (ignored along
with start/end).

business_hours_start.description:
BusinessHoursStart/End are local-time strings "HH:MM" in the agent's
Timezone. Both empty = 24/7 bot. When set, the bot silently skips AI
processing outside the window; a human picking up the conversation
still works (IsBotPaused semantics unchanged).

hide_ai_identity.description:
HideAIIdentity = true (default) prevents the bot from admitting it's
an AI/virtual assistant, so customers keep conversing as if with a
human attendant. Flipping it off lets the bot acknowledge its nature
when directly asked.

learn_from_humans.description: analyze human replies to build personality

silent_on_unknown.description:
SilentOnUnknown = true (default) switches the bot to a silent
handoff when it would otherwise admit it doesn't know — the bot
emits the [HANDOFF] sentinel instead of a reply; the pipeline
swallows it and pauses the bot so a human takes over without the
customer seeing a "I don't know" message. Off = bot produces a
warm apology in the customer's language (legacy behavior).

description.description: One-liner shown under the dropdown option

name.description: Suggested agent name ("Clara, assistente da clínica")

segment.description: Free-text category shown on the UI card

period_days.description:
PeriodDays mirrors the query param so the client can sanity-check
what the server actually ran (values outside 7|30|90 get clamped).

decision_maker.description:
DecisionMaker is the ROLE to reach, which decides how the approach is
written far more than the segment does. A message to a purchasing
manager and one to a clinical director share almost no sentences.

keywords.description:
Keywords is what actually reaches the prospecting source. Derived from
the fields above when the audience is created, then editable — the
person doing the work knows their market's vocabulary better than any
generator does.

regions.description: Regions are cities, states, or whatever the customer thinks in.

segment.description:
Segment is the kind of business, in the customer's own words:
"clínicas de diagnóstico por imagem", not a CNAE code. The code is a
filter; this is what a salesperson would say out loud.

size.description:
Size narrows by scale — "de 10 a 50 leitos". Free text, because every
market measures size differently and a dropdown would be wrong for
most of them.

suggested.description:
Suggested marks an audience a model proposed rather than a human
typed. Kept visible: "a IA sugeriu" is information, and a suggestion
presented as the customer's own decision is a small lie that erodes
trust in every other suggestion.

unexplored.description:
Unexplored flags the one suggestion deliberately chosen for being
adjacent rather than obvious — the "você talvez não viu" slot. Exactly
one per suggestion round: two would be a list, and a list of things
you have not considered is just noise.

ip.description:
IP + UserAgent record the request origin (US-073). Nil for
background/worker writes that have no inbound HTTP request.

daily_cap.description:
DailyCap bounds a bad day. Even a perfect model with a wrong prompt is
only allowed to be wrong this many times before a human has to look.

enabled_at.description: EnabledAt / EnabledBy is who turned it on, for the day somebody asks.

min_score.description:
MinScore is the lead quality floor. Cold outbound to a badly-matched
lead is what burns a domain, and it is the case a tired human catches
and an eager one does not.

offered_at.description:
OfferedAt records when we last asked. Nil means never — the offer is
made once and not nagged.

unedited_streak.description:
UneditedStreak counts consecutive approvals sent EXACTLY as drafted.
Reset by any edit or discard: the streak is evidence that the model
writes what this person would have written, and an edit is that
evidence expiring.

about.description:
About is what the company does, in its own words. Feeds every prompt
and every template.

allowed_claims.description:
AllowedClaims are the things a salesperson MAY say. Listed rather than
implied so a new seller has a source instead of a guess.

forbidden_claims.description:
ForbiddenClaims are the things nobody may say, at any level. In
healthcare this is where "cure", "no side effects" and "approved by the
regulator" live when they are not true — and where a
wrong sentence stops being a style problem and becomes a regulatory
one.

logo_url.description: LogoURL and colours dress the email templates.

tone_of_voice.description: ToneOfVoice is how it speaks — "direct, jargon-free, informal".

imap_last_error.description:
IMAP poll health, derived response-only fields for email channels
(read from email_imap_cursors on GET /channels). A failure count above
zero means replies are NOT being read — a revoked Google grant or a
changed password shows up here and nowhere else, so the dashboard can
say "reconnect" instead of the mailbox silently going quiet.

is_fully_configured.description:
IsFullyConfigured is a derived response-only field. True when the
channel has all credentials needed to actually talk to Meta (e.g.
WhatsApp needs phone_number_id + waba_id + access_token). Lets the
Flutter UI distinguish "stub channel" from "ready channel" without
reading masked config strings. Not persisted.

token_expires_at.description:
TokenExpiresAt / TokenExpiringSoon are derived response-only
fields for channels whose access token dies of old age (Instagram
long-lived tokens last ~60 days). The stamp lives in the config
JSONB as `token_expires_at` (written when the token is set or
rotated); these surface it so the dashboard can flag "reconnect
soon" before inbound DMs silently stop. Not persisted as columns.

customers.description:
Customers is how many DISTINCT customers bought both. Distinct on
purpose: one customer ordering the same pair twelve times is one
pattern, not twelve.

product.description:
Product and Partner are normalised item labels, not ids: most sales
carry free text, and waiting for a catalogue match would mean learning
nothing until every product is registered.

product_customers.description:
ProductCustomers is how many bought the first item at all — the
denominator that turns a count into a rate.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
Suggestion is at most ONE copilot nudge. Singular by design: a screen
with three suggestions is a screen where all three get ignored.

prompt.description:
Prompt is what gets sent to the copilot when tapped — the whole point
is that the suggestion is one tap from being done, not a hint the user
has to retype.

active_leads.description: ActiveLeads excludes won/lost — the work actually in front of the user.

meetings.description:
Meetings booked in the period. Real now that the sales event log
records them (it was deliberately absent from the first command centre
while nothing measured it).

period_label.description:
Period names the window the last two tiles cover, because "ganhos"
with no period is a number nobody can check.

untouched_targets.description:
UntouchedTargets is how many establishments in the account's territory
hold the equipment it sells and have never been approached.

The size of what is being LOST, which no other tile shows: the other
four all count work already in hand, so an account with one lead and a
whole state in front of it looked identical to one that had worked the
state through.

Deliberately NOT a money figure. CNES says how many machines an
establishment has, never what a deal is worth — inventing a ticket to
fill a currency column would be the product guessing.

won_gross_cents.description: WonGrossCents is what closed in the period.

amount_cents.description: AmountCents is the commission before splits.

base_cents.description: BaseCents is what the percentage was applied to.

explanation.description: Explanation says in words what happened, in the customer's language.

milestone_cents.description: MilestoneCents is the fixed bonus, when a target was reached.

rate_percent.description:
RatePercent is the rate that ended up applying, after tiers and the
repurchase override.

shares.description:
Shares is the split, when the rule has one. Empty means it all goes to
the sale's own salesperson.

warning.description:
Warning flags a payout somebody should look at before it goes out —
most importantly, commission on a sale that lost money.

seller_email.description: Joined on listing reads for display; empty elsewhere.

cycle.description:
Cycle is the month the line belongs to, "YYYY-MM", resolved in the
ACCOUNT's timezone — a sale closed at 21:00 on the 31st belongs to the
month the salesperson thinks it does.

explanation.description:
Explanation is the sentence the engine wrote when it calculated this.
Stored rather than recomputed: the rule may have changed since, and the
answer to "why this number" has to be the reason it was ACTUALLY paid.

note.description: Note is what a human typed when adjusting or paying.

role.description:
Role is the split role this line pays ("closer", "quem indicou"), empty
when the whole commission goes to the sale's own salesperson.

rule_id.description:
RuleID is which rule produced this. Kept even after the rule is
deleted, because "why was I paid this?" outlives the rule.

sale_id.description: SaleID is empty on a milestone and on a manual adjustment.

seller_name.description:
SellerName is filled on read for display. Not persisted — a name is
somebody's current name, not a fact about a payout.

seller_user_id.description:
SellerUserID is who gets paid. Never empty: a line nobody is owed is a
line that should not exist.

rate_percent.description: RatePercent is the flat rate, used when there are no tiers.

repurchase_rate_percent.description:
RepurchaseRatePercent pays differently for a customer who already
bought. Nil means "same as a new sale" — which is different from zero,
and a company that genuinely pays nothing on repurchase has to say so.

scope_id.description:
ScopeID is the seller/team/product the scope points at. Empty for
global.

tiers.description: Tiers, when present, REPLACE the flat rate.

effective_rate_percent.description:
EffectiveRatePercent is the commission over the whole month's GROSS —
the number an owner actually needs, because it is what the rule costs
the company regardless of which base it was written against.

role.description:
Role is free text the company recognises ("closer", "quem indicou",
"gerente"). Not an enum: every company names these differently, and an
enum would force somebody to pick the wrong word for their own process.

share_percent.description: SharePercent of the commission, not of the sale.

pending_cents.description:
PendingCents is what is still owed — the number the admin is about to
transfer, and the only one that changes when they mark the month paid.

sales_cents.description:
SalesCents and SalesCount are what the commission was earned ON, so the
statement can be checked against the invoices without a second screen.

total_cents.description: TotalCents is everything on the statement, paid and pending.

warnings.description:
Warnings are the lines somebody should look at before paying: a sale
that lost money, a commission with no rule, a negative total.

from_cents.description:
FromCents is the period total at which the tier starts. The first tier
normally starts at 0.

rate_percent.description: RatePercent is the percentage of the base. 2.5 means 2.5%.

company_name.description:
CompanyName is the organization the person is at. Kept on the contact
rather than in `companies` (which nothing reads): a CSV row "Clínica
Aurora;Marina" used to lose the clinic the moment it had a person.

opted_out_at.description:
OptedOutAt, when non-nil, means the contact explicitly asked to stop
receiving broadcast messages (LGPD Art. 18 / CAN-SPAM). The timestamp
is kept for audit; campaigns must filter these out at creation time.

booking_url.description:
BookingURL is the calendar page where a prospect books a call
(Google Calendar appointment schedule). Sales-led since 2026-08-19:
the product shows no price list; the conversation is the offer. Empty
when unconfigured, and the clients then fall back to WhatsApp/e-mail.

ai_proposal.description:
AIProposal is the model's reading, verbatim. Never written by a human and
never used to drive an alert on its own.

amendments.description: Amendments is filled on a detail read: the chain in force, oldest first.

auto_renewal.description:
AutoRenewal + NoticeDays is the most expensive pair of facts in the
document: miss the window and the contract renews itself.

last_adjusted_on.description:
LastAdjustedOn is when the price was actually raised. Without it an
accumulation would run from the contract's start forever and double-count
every adjustment already applied.

object_path.description:
ObjectPath is the PDF in the private bucket. Empty when the contract was
registered from pasted text.

parent_contract_id.description:
ParentContractID chains an amendment (aditivo) to the contract it
changes; Version is its place in that chain.

price_registry.description:
The price registry (ata de registro de preços). A public body committed to
buy, the supplier delivered part of it, and the remaining balance expires
with the ata — pre-approved revenue nobody goes back for.

redacted.description:
Redacted says fields were REMOVED for the caller's role. Without this
flag a redacted value_cents of 0 reads as "this contract is free", which
is a worse lie than showing nothing — the client renders "oculto" only
because the server admitted it hid something.

registry_balance_on.description:
RegistryBalanceOn is when the balance was last known. A balance with no
date is a number nobody can trust: "R$80k left as of last week" and
"R$80k left as of a year ago" are different facts.

starts_on.description:
StartsOn/EndsOn are calendar dates: a contract runs on days, and putting
a timezone on "vence em 31/12" only creates off-by-one arguments.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
Adjustment is what the price is owed: the accumulated index since the base
date, and the new value it implies. Absent when the contract states no
adjustment month — a price nobody agreed to raise gets no suggestion.

base_date.description:
BaseDate is what the accumulation counts from: the last time the price was
actually raised, or the contract's start when it never was.

current_value_cents.description:
CurrentValueCents is the contract's value today and SuggestedValueCents
what it becomes with the accumulation applied. Suggested is absent when
the accumulation was incomplete or there is no value to raise: a
suggested price built on a partial series is a number somebody would
quote to a customer.

due_on.description: DueOn is the next adjustment date the contract states.

gain_cents.description:
GainCents is the difference — the money on the table, which is the only
number that makes anybody open the alert.

overdue.description:
Overdue says the date has passed with no adjustment recorded — the state
that is quietly costing money every month it stays true.

contract_title.description:
ContractTitle is filled on read, so a list of alerts is readable without a
second fetch per row.

lead_id.description: LeadID is the renewal lead this alert produced, when it produced one.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description: Kind says which of the three leaks this plugged.

document.description:
Document is the CNPJ/CPF as printed. Kept as text, unnormalised: what
matters is matching the paper, and "reformatting" a document number is
how a typo becomes invisible.

role.description:
Role is free text the document uses ("contratante", "contratada",
"fiadora"). Not an enum: contracts name these however they like, and an
enum would force the extractor to pick the wrong word.

amount_cents.description: AmountCents is a fixed penalty, when the clause states one.

percent.description:
Percent is the rate when the clause states one; zero when the penalty is
a fixed amount or a non-monetary consequence.

trigger.description:
Trigger is what sets it off ("atraso no pagamento", "rescisão
antecipada").

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents is what a HUMAN says was collected — never the computed figure.
The accumulated index is what was OWED; what was agreed differs every time
somebody negotiates, and the ledger has to match the invoice.

detail.description: Detail is the clause behind it, when there is one worth quoting.

due_on.description:
DueOn is when it becomes somebody's problem. Nil for a standing term
(exclusivity) — and a flag with no date cannot become a scheduled alert,
which is honest rather than a task on an invented day.

money_at_stake_cents.description:
MoneyAtStakeCents is what acting on it is worth. Zero when the flag is a
constraint rather than an amount.

scheduled.description:
Scheduled says an alert already exists for this flag, so the UI offers
"agendado" instead of a second "agendar".

title.description:
Title is the sentence a person reads: "renova sozinho se você não avisar
até 30/01/2027". Written here rather than in the client so the app, the
digest, the push and the co-pilot all say the same thing.

covers_until.description: CoversUntil is the newest message this brief accounts for.

model.description:
Model is recorded so a bad summary is traceable to a routing change
rather than argued about.

inbox_category.description:
Inbox triage (§6.10 camada 3). Empty for a conversation classified
before the feature existed, and for every channel that is not a shared
mailbox — the inbox falls back to chronological, which is correct for
a chat.

lead_id.description:
Lead context for the inbox (US-M024): which pipeline stage this
contact sits in, so an attendant answering a message knows whether
they are talking to a stranger or to a deal in negotiation. All
three are empty when the contact is not a lead — the inbox works
exactly as before for pure support conversations.

lead_stage_name.description:
LeadStageName is the customer's own column name. Empty for leads
created before the board existed; LeadStatus is then the fallback,
because a chip reading the canonical status is still more useful
than no chip.

unread_count.description:
UnreadCount is how many customer (inbound) messages nobody opened
yet — messages.read_at IS NULL, stamped by POST /conversations/:id/read.
The tile used to derive "unread" from status = pending_human, which
is a different fact (waiting on a human, not unseen).

because.description:
Because names the item they DO buy, so the salesperson can say why.
A suggestion with no reason is a guess the customer can hear.

confidence.description: Confidence is the observed rate among this account's own customers.

suggest.description: Suggest is the item they have NOT bought.

company.description:
Company is the organization; Name is the person at it. Both travel, even
though only one is needed, because the preview should say which column it
read rather than merging them into a single label.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate marks the "já está na sua base" case structurally, so the
client renders it as the fact it is (the existing customer stays)
instead of with the same error icon as an unreadable phone.

line.description:
Line is the 1-based line in the original file, header included, so a
problem points at the row the person is looking at in Excel.

phone.description:
Phone is E.164 when it could be read at all, otherwise empty with a
Problem set. Email is lower-cased.

problem.description:
Problem is empty when the row may create a contact. When it is not, the
row still travels — a silently dropped line is a customer the person
believes they imported.

detail.description: Detail explains a kept or failed record in the user's terms.

Detail is the evidence behind it, for the seller and the model — never
invented, because this is the account's own text.

label.description: Label is the claim in a few words ("Assistência em Cuiabá, 24h").

product_id.description:
ProductID scopes it to one product. Empty is the common case: most
differentiators belong to the COMPANY (assistance in the state, parts in
stock) and apply to everything it sells.

imported_at.description:
ImportedAt and DismissedAt are kept apart because "not now" is not
"already done": collapsing them would either re-offer what she refused or
hide what she has not decided.

last_subject.description:
LastSubject is the newest sighting's envelope subject (issue #292):
what the relationship was last about, feeding the lead dossier so a
draft can pick the thread back up instead of opening cold.

sent_count.description:
SentCount, FirstSentAt and LastSentAt are the ranking signal. Somebody
emailed 40 times across two years is a customer; somebody emailed once is
a stranger who asked a question.

detail.description: Detail is human-readable and specific. Shown verbatim.

weight.description:
Weight contributes to the score. Kept on the signal so a change of
policy is a change of numbers, not of structure.

diagnostic.description:
Diagnostic is the remote server's verbatim refusal, so a person asking
"why can't I email them?" gets an answer instead of a policy.

opened.description:
Opened is a WEAK signal and labelled as such wherever it is shown:
Apple Mail Privacy Protection pre-fetches images, inflating opens by
roughly half. Kept because the trend still means something; never
decisive on its own.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
EmailWarmup is a derived response-only field for email channels: the
mailbox's warmup state and today's send budget, computed by the SAME
rules the send gate applies, so the screen and the refusal can never
disagree. Not persisted.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the file was cut at the ceiling, so an auditor reading
"50000 rows" knows it was not the whole table.

userEmail.description:
UserEmail is stored rather than joined at read time: this row has to
survive the person leaving, and "who exported the customer list" is
exactly the question asked after somebody leaves.

complete.description:
Complete is false when the series was missing at least one month in the
range. A partial accumulation is NOT reported as a percentage anybody
should negotiate with — see MissingMonths.

from.description:
From is the first month INCLUDED in the accumulation (the month after the
base date) and To the last.

missing_months.description:
MissingMonths names what was absent, so the screen can say "faltam dois
meses da série" instead of showing a number that is quietly low.

months.description:
Months is how many months were compounded — the sanity check a person
does out loud ("doze meses de IPCA, faz sentido").

percent.description:
Percent is the compounded variation, rounded to two decimals: 4.83 means
the price may rise 4.83%.

similarity.description:
Similarity is the cosine similarity of this chunk against the query
embedding, in [0, 1]. Only populated by Search(); zero for listings.
The AgentRunner drops chunks under a threshold so low-relevance
results don't confidently hallucinate their way into the prompt.

anticipated_objections.description:
AnticipatedObjections is what the matcher call expects THIS customer
to push back with, already answered: [{label, counter}]. Shown on the
approval card and injected into the draft so the text can preempt it.

board_pos.description:
BoardPos is the manually chosen rank inside the column (fractional
ranking, see ComputeBoardPos). Nil = never manually placed: the card
keeps the automatic most-stalled-first order, AFTER every placed one.
Written only by a drag (FunnelStageRepository.MoveLead) and cleared by
the column's reset-order action.

contact_address.description:
ContactAddress is the same kind of display-only join, but always the
ADDRESS the message would go to — never the name. The approval step
needs it: a name cannot catch a wrong number.

contact_label.description:
ContactLabel is a DISPLAY-ONLY join (never persisted): the human name,
phone or email behind ContactID. Every outbound approval shows the
operator who the message will reach, and a ULID answers that question
with nothing.

matched_products.description:
MatchedProducts is which of the account's products this lead's offer
is about, and why: [{product_id, name, reason}]. Chosen by the offer
matcher against the catalogue; the draft, the card and the approval
screen read the same pick. Empty until drafted.

owner_user_id.description:
OwnerUserID is the salesperson responsible for this lead (US-F009).
Empty/nil = unassigned, which stays visible to the whole team — a
freshly prospected lead belongs to nobody yet.

stage_id.description:
StageID is the Kanban column the card sits in (US-M008). Nil for
leads created before the board existed, or by paths that know nothing
about it (inbound, prospecting) — those resolve onto the column
matching their canonical status.

external_message_id.description:
ExternalMessageID is the provider-side id (e.g. WhatsApp wamid) used
to dedupe webhook retries. Nil for outbound messages and for channels
that don't expose stable ids (legacy Telegram rows, seeded data).

failed_at.description:
FailedAt/FailedReason surface an outbound send failure (SDK/HTTP
layer or a later delivery-status webhook) so the dashboard bubble
can render "send failed" instead of silently looking delivered.
Nil on inbound rows and on outbound rows that sent fine.

input_tokens.description:
US-030: per-message AI token accounting + estimated provider cost.
Populated only on AI-generated outbound messages; nil everywhere
else (inbound, human replies, system messages). Token counts come
from the provider's usage report with a len(text)/4 fallback;
ProviderCostUSD is a coarse list-price estimate (see services.ProviderCostUSD).

media_url.description: CDN / signed URL for media files

token_estimated.description:
US-042: true when the input/output token counts came from the
len(text)/4 fallback because the provider omitted usage (e.g. a
truncated streamed response). Lets A/B attribution + billing discount
estimates instead of trusting them as exact provider counts. Nil on
non-AI messages and on rows written before the flag existed.

transcript.description:
Transcript is the cached Whisper/Gemini output for audio/voice
messages. Nil when the attendant hasn't requested transcription yet;
empty string when the transcriber ran but returned nothing so we
don't keep retrying the same silent clip.

is_inline.description:
IsInline marks message furniture (a signature logo, a tracking pixel)
rather than a document someone meant to send.

average_score.description: AverageScore is the mean raw 0-10 rating; 0 when there are no responses.

score.description: Score is the rounded NPS in [-100, 100]; 0 when there are no responses.

audience_names.description:
AudienceNames are the ones the person kept. Kept as names rather than ids
because they are created at the end of the step, and a draft that
referenced rows that do not exist yet would be a draft that cannot be
resumed.

website.description:
Website is the highest-leverage single input: one URL usually answers
what they sell and to whom, which is why the company step asks for it.

role.description:
Role is "assistant" or "user". Not a model conversation — the assistant
turns are the machine's scripted questions, and storing them keeps the
screen from having to re-derive what was already asked.

account_name.description:
AccountName mirrors accounts.name. The onboarding wizard pre-fills
the "Qual o nome da sua empresa?" field with this value. For
social-login (Google/Meta) accounts it starts as the user's
personal name — the new step 0 is specifically here so they can
replace it with their real business name.

products_added.description:
The SALES milestones — what "getting started" means for this product.
Products first because nothing else works without knowing what she sells;
a proposal last because the three before it are setup and this is the first
time the product did the thing it exists for.

team_invited.description:
TeamInvited: somebody besides the owner has a seat. The seller who
approves the offers is usually not the person who signed up.

skippable.description: Skippable is false only for the company step.

widget.description:
Widget tells the client what to draw: a plain input, editable chips, or
the channel tiles. The server decides, so a new step does not need a
client release to be answerable.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
Briefing is what the overnight run produced (K2), when there is one
worth telling somebody about. Nil is the normal case — most mornings
there was nothing to draft, and "0 abordagens prontas" every day is how
a good habit becomes a dismissed banner.

stopped_reason.description:
StoppedReason is why the night gave up, when it did. Empty covers both
a normal run and a legitimately quiet one — an account with nobody
left to write to has not failed.

used_batch.description:
UsedBatch says whether the provider's batch endpoint did the work. The
whole cost argument for running overnight rests on it, and an account
whose provider has none gets the convenience without the discount — which
the briefing must not imply otherwise.

enabled.description:
Enabled is opt-IN. This spends the account's AI allowance without anyone
asking for it that night, so it has to be a decision somebody made.

funnel_id.description: FunnelID narrows the run. Empty means every active funnel.

last_run_on.description:
LastRunOn is the account-local date of the last run, so a worker tick
cannot run the same night twice.

nightly_cap.description:
NightlyCap is how many to draft per night, on top of (never instead of)
the plan's monthly allowance.

run_hour.description: RunHour is the local hour the run starts, in the ACCOUNT's timezone.

carteira_count.description:
CarteiraCount is the number of customer accounts currently linked
to this seller (accounts.seller_user_id).

share_url.description:
ShareURL is the full marketing-site signup link for SellerRefCode
(webBaseURL + /register?ref=CODE) — built by the use case so the
app never hardcodes the site origin.

customer_name.description:
CustomerName is the point. Empty only when the underlying record
genuinely has no contact — then the client falls back to the detail.

deep_link.description:
DeepLink is where the work happens, built server-side so a new action
kind needs no client release to be actionable.

detail.description:
Detail is the specific fact, already assembled ("assinou dia 3, venceu
ontem"). Not a template for the client to fill: the server knows which
of six shapes this row is.

due_on.description: DueOn is the calendar deadline, for the actions that have one.

money_at_stake_cents.description:
MoneyAtStakeCents is what acting on it is worth. Zero means the action
carries no amount (an unowned lead, a draft) — NOT that it is worth
nothing, which is why ranking never divides by it.

since_at.description:
SinceAt is when this started waiting. Drives the age ranking for the
moneyless actions and the "há 4 dias" the row shows.

target_id.description:
TargetID is what the action is about (a lead, a signature request, an
alert). Also the dismissal key, so a snooze survives the row being
recomputed from scratch on the next load.

is_listed.description:
IsListed gates the public catalogue (GET /plans). FALSE keeps the
row alive for accounts already on it (FKs, invoices) while hiding
it from signup/upgrade flows — used to retire Partner (US-001,
vendedores v3).

max_ai_drafts_per_month.description:
The two AI operations a single request can spend in bulk (K4):
`draft_approaches_batch` fills a whole queue, and the scanned-contract
path sends entire PDFs to a multimodal model.

max_broadcast_messages_per_month.description: Broadcast caps — 0 means the plan does not permit broadcasts.

max_daily_ai_tokens.description:
MaxDailyAITokens caps AI tokens per calendar day (US-025). 0 means
"use the platform default" — see EffectiveMaxDailyAITokens. A
contract plan can set a higher explicit value.

max_history_messages.description:
MaxHistoryMessages caps how many recent conversation messages are
replayed into the AI prompt each turn (US-024). 0 means "use the
platform default" — see EffectiveMaxHistoryMessages. Older turns are
folded into conversations.summary so context isn't lost. A contract
plan can raise this for richer multi-turn coherence.

max_leads_per_month.description:
SDR tier caps (US-M013). The product sells prospecting, so these are
the numbers a customer actually shops on. 0 keeps the platform-wide
meaning: "not allowed" on a self-serve plan, "use the account
override" on a contract plan (see resolveLimit).

overage_conversation_cents.description:
Overage metering (Mission 8 pricing revamp).
OverageConversationCents is the per-extra-conversation rate in
centavos BRL once the plan's franchise is exhausted.
OverageCapMultiplier caps total overage at N× the plan price
in the same billing cycle (typically 2.00; 1.50 for Partner).

stripe_price_id_annual.description:
StripePriceIDAnnual is the Stripe Price id for the yearly recurring
charge (US-169). nil/empty means the plan has no annual option —
checkout then falls back to the monthly price. Contract plans keep
both nil.

accessories.description:
Accessories are the optional items offered FOR this product. They exist
so a "Válvula reguladora" stops arriving as a product of its own — an
accessory is a row in the catalogue nobody can sell alone.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate marks the "já está no catálogo" case STRUCTURALLY. It is a
fact, not a mistake — the existing product stays, nothing is
overwritten — and the client needs to render it neutrally instead of
painting it with the same error icon as an unreadable price. The text
in Problem stays for humans; this flag is for the renderer.

line.description:
Line is the 1-based line in the original file, header included, so a
problem can be pointed at the row the person is looking at in Excel.

page.description:
Page is the 1-based brochure page the row was read from, so a human can
open the PDF and check the model's source. 0 on CSV rows.

problem.description:
Problem is empty when the row is importable. When it is not, the row still
travels: a silently dropped line is a product the person believes they
imported.

sku.description:
PDF-brochure origin fields. Empty on CSV rows — the CSV has no columns
for them. They travel to the preview so the person can check what the
model read; on confirmation they land in the product's attributes.

source_id.description:
SourceID / SourcePage point back at the archived brochure: which file,
which page. Empty on CSV rows.

specs.description:
Specs is the brochure's technical block, transcribed rather than
summarised: dimensions, power, ranges, materials, what ships with it.
A distributor answering "cabe na minha UTI?" needs the sheet, and the
old extraction threw it away — 126 characters on average survived.

standards.description:
Standards are the norms and certifications the brochure cites
(NBR IEC 60601, ANVISA…). In this market they are half the argument in
a bid, and they were being dropped.

total_referred.description: Total accounts that signed up with this account's referral code.

total_rewarded.description: Of those, how many converted to a paid plan and triggered a reward.

contact_id.description:
ContactID is empty for an account-wide date — a sector day applies to
the whole portfolio, and duplicating it per contact would mean six
hundred rows saying the same thing.

due_at.description: DueAt drives a ONE-OFF date (maintenance). Nil on a recurring one.

last_fired_year.description:
LastFiredYear stops a recurring date from firing twice in one year —
a worker that ticks daily would otherwise send a birthday greeting
every day of the lead-time window.

month.description:
Month and Day drive a RECURRING date. Year is deliberately absent:
what matters about a birthday is that it comes round.

gross_cents.description:
GrossCents of the last order, so an approach can offer the same
quantity rather than asking what they want.

product_key.description:
ProductKey identifies WHICH product of that sale this prediction is
about (product_id, else the normalised description) — a sale with two
cycled products yields two candidates and two nudges.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
Visibility governs whether teammates can see an OWNED lead. Mutation
is always owner-or-manager regardless of this value.

warnings.description:
Warnings names the sections that failed to load. A blown aggregate
degrades to a named gap instead of taking the screen down or, worse,
rendering as an empty section that reads like "you did nothing".

ai_cost_cents.description:
AICostCents is the AI spend attributable to this channel, converted
from the immutable per-message stamp at the platform rate. It is NOT
the whole cost of the channel — see SDRCostDisclosure.

channel.description:
Channel is the channel TYPE (whatsapp, telegram, sms…), not one
channel row: a customer with three WhatsApp numbers thinks in
"WhatsApp".

ai_only.description:
AIOnly is always true today. It is a field rather than a doc comment
so the UI renders the caveat from the payload and can stop when
carrier metering exists.

currency.description: Currency the cost figures are in.

rate_cents.description: RateCents is the USD→BRL rate applied to the AI stamp.

better.description:
Better is nil when there is nothing to compare (no previous period
data) — a first-week account should see "—", not a fake +100%.

conversion_from_entry.description:
ConversionFromEntry is count/first-step, the number a salesperson
actually quotes ("de cada 100 leads, 4 fecham").

conversion_from_previous.description:
ConversionFromPrevious is count/previous as a 0..1 fraction. Nil on
the first step (nothing to convert from) and whenever the previous
step is zero.

incomplete.description:
Incomplete flags a step that counts MORE leads than the step above
it. That is not a funnel — it means the rung above was never
recorded for some leads (a sale entered by hand, an approach sent
before instrumentation). Surfaced rather than clamped: a silently
capped number is a lie, and this one is a genuine data-quality fact
the operator can act on.

metric.description: Metric is the machine name, and doubles as the drill-down key.

gross_cents.description: GrossCents is the sale this lead produced, when it produced one.

from.description:
From is inclusive, To exclusive — the half-open convention every
aggregation in this codebase uses, so a row on the boundary is
counted exactly once.

timezone.description:
Timezone names the frame the bounds were computed in, so a number can
be checked rather than trusted.

seller_user_id.description:
SellerUserID is empty for work nobody owns. Reported as its own row
rather than dropped — unowned leads piling up IS the finding.

value_cents.description:
ValueCents sums the disclosed values of the signals. Tenders that did
not disclose a value contribute zero, so this is a floor, never a
total — DisclosedCount says how much of the set it covers.

won_gross_cents.description:
WonGrossCents is what the wins were worth. A strategy with a lower
win rate and bigger deals can be the better one, and a screen that
only shows rates hides that.

avg_reply_seconds.description:
AvgReplySeconds is nil when nobody replied. An average over zero
replies rendered as "0s" would be the most flattering possible lie.

researched.description:
Researched is enrichment runs in the window, reported here rather than
as a funnel rung because researching is optional — see
SDRFunnelLadder.

confirmed_by_user_id.description:
ConfirmedByUserID is who approved an AI-extracted sale. Empty on a
manual one, where the person entering it IS the confirmation.

contact_id.description:
ContactID is who bought. Required: a sale with no customer cannot
feed a portfolio, which is half the reason this table exists.

cost_cents.description:
CostCents is what the goods or delivery cost. Zero is a legitimate
value for a service with no marginal cost — and a dangerous default
for a distributor, which is why the UI asks rather than assumes.

cycle_days.description:
CycleDays is how long until this customer is likely to need it again.
The single field the repurchase engine (F3) runs on — "200 caixas de
luvas, ciclo ~30d" is a prediction somebody can act on, and a sale
with no cycle is one the engine will never resurface.

gross_cents.description:
The three amounts, in cents, in Currency. Integers throughout: money
in floats accumulates error, and a cent lost per sale is an argument
with a salesperson every month.

lead_id.description:
LeadID links the deal it came from, when there was one. Optional —
plenty of sales come from a phone call nobody logged.

seller_user_id.description:
SellerUserID is who gets the commission. Optional: a house account
sale has no salesperson, and inventing one would pay somebody for
work they did not do.

tax_cents.description:
TaxCents is what leaves for the government. Separate from cost
because a Brazilian company's tax burden is not a cost of goods and
is not negotiable the same way.

found.description:
Found is false when the conversation holds no sale. Explicit rather
than an empty struct, so "não encontrei uma venda aqui" is an answer
the UI can show instead of a blank form.

question.description:
Question is the confirmation to put in front of the human, in their
words: "fechou 200 cx de luvas, ciclo ~30d?". The whole interaction is
this one sentence, so the model writes it rather than the UI
assembling one from fields.

product_id.description: ProductID links the catalogue when the item matches something in it.

unit_cents.description:
UnitCents is optional: plenty of deals are agreed as a total, and
demanding a unit price would make somebody invent one.

converted_conversation_id.description:
Platform conversation that converted this inbound lead (US-004
stamp) — the co-pilot deep link (US-015). Nil for ?ref= signups.

last_cycle_net_profit_cents.description:
Last closed cycle: computed net profit, the seller's TOTAL
commission on the account (profit share + additive bonuses) and
the profit-share rate/reason actually applied.

has_payment_history.description:
HasPaymentHistory is true when the account ever had a Stripe
subscription (US-014): such an organically paying account can only
be converted when the lead conversation's contact provably belongs
to it — otherwise an attendant could steal attribution of any
existing customer.

signature.description:
Signature overrides the company signature — the one thing that SHOULD
be personal, since it carries a name and a phone number.

tone_note.description:
ToneNote is how this person talks, appended to the company's voice
rather than replacing it.

seller_email.description: Joined on listing reads for display; empty elsewhere.

is_seller.description:
IsSeller is the EXPLICIT owner grant (review-fixes US-014): only
flagged users reach the /seller panel, mint ref codes, have their
codes resolve at signup or get stamped by convert-lead. DEFAULT
FALSE — a row created as a side-effect (pix key, activity clause)
never makes someone payable by itself.

revenue_cents.description: Full profit breakdown of the account's cycle (account_monthly_profit).

channel_id.description:
ChannelID scopes channel-level signals (whatsapp_ban_risk emits one
suggestion per RED number, review-fixes US-022) so dismissing one
channel's risk never hides another's. Nil on account-level types.

conversation_id.description:
Platform conversation with this client (the one the convert action
stamped, US-015) — lets the feed open the chat with a pre-filled
template. Nil when no conversation ever existed (?ref= signup).

business_hours_only.description:
BusinessHoursOnly holds sends until the next working hour. A cold
email at 03:14 reads as a machine, which is exactly what it must not.

stop_on_reply.description:
StopOnReply defaults TRUE and there is deliberately no UI to turn it
off. It is exposed as a field only so the rule is visible in the
payload the editor renders at the top of the screen.

current_step.description:
CurrentStep is the NEXT step to run, 1-based. Zero means nothing has
run yet.

next_run_at.description:
NextRunAt is when the worker should look at this again. Nil for a
finished or paused enrollment.

delay_hours.description:
DelayHours is how long AFTER the previous step this one fires. On a
wait step it is the whole content of the step.

subject.description: Subject and Body let a step carry its own text instead of a template.

task_title.description:
TaskTitle is what the human is asked to do. Required on a human task:
"tarefa" with no instruction is a notification nobody can action.

template_id.description:
TemplateID points at an email template, or at an approved WhatsApp
template name for a WhatsApp step. Empty on a human task or a wait.

reached.description: Reached counts enrollments that got this far.

replied.description:
Replied counts the ones that answered AFTER this step and before the
next — which is what "este passo funciona" actually means.

cnaes.description:
CNAEs narrow by the buyer's economic activity, when the source
publishes it.

derived_from_catalog.description:
DerivedFromCatalog marks keywords the seeder derived from the
account's own products, as opposed to typed by a person. The signals
screen phrases itself as "matches what you sell" — that claim is only
honest for derived watches, so the UI shows the origin.

keywords.description:
Keywords match the tender's title and description. Any match counts —
a supplier of monitors sells to "monitor multiparâmetro" and to
"monitorização", and demanding all terms would find nothing.

min_value_cents.description:
MinValueCents filters out the noise floor. A tender for R$ 800 of
office supplies is not worth a salesperson's morning.

states.description:
States narrows by region, because a supplier who cannot deliver to
Acre does not want to read about Acre.

contact_id.description:
ContactID is who this is with. Required for the signature to become a
Sale: a sale with no customer feeds no portfolio.

provider_doc_token.description: ProviderDocToken is the document's id at the provider.

sale_id.description: SaleID is the Sale this produced. Its presence is the idempotency guard.

value_cents.description:
ValueCents is what the signature is worth. Zero means track it and
register NO sale — a signed document with no value is not a sale, and
inventing one puts a number in somebody's commission.

phone.description: Phone is E.164 when present. The provider may notify by WhatsApp with it.

sign_url.description:
SignURL is the individual signing link. Handed to a person deliberately,
never posted to a customer by a machine: it IS the authority to sign.

arguments.description:
Arguments are what to lead with. Ordered by the author, because the
order IS the argument.

author_user_id.description:
AuthorUserID is recognition, and recognition is what makes a
salesperson contribute one. A strategy with no visible author is a
company document; one with a name on it is somebody's method.

channel_mix.description:
ChannelMix is the plan: which channels in which order. Free text
rather than a structured cadence, because a strategy describes an
intent and a Sequence implements it — conflating them would make
every wording change a migration.

icp.description: ICP is who this is for, in the seller's own words.

objections.description:
Objections map what they say to what to answer. The part of a
strategy that a new salesperson actually reads.

sequence_id.description:
SequenceID links the cadence that implements this strategy, when one
exists. Optional: a strategy is worth writing down before anyone has
built the automation for it.

triggers.description:
Triggers are the moments this strategy applies: "publicou edital",
"trocou de diretor clínico".

version.description:
Version is bumped when the CONTENT changes. "Essa estratégia converte
14%" is meaningless if the arguments were rewritten twice since the
number was earned — the same reason email templates version.

approaches.description: Approaches counts leads that were written to under this version.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_do.description:
Territory: nil means "don't touch". To clear, send {"uf": ""}.
Otherwise UF is required (2 letters), cities optional.
Author is who said it, resolved from the raw sender. See TimelineAuthor.

author_name.description:
AuthorName is the human behind an outbound reply, when there is one. Empty
for the customer and for the bot, whose names the row already carries.

failed_at.description:
FailedAt/FailedReason expose the channel adapter's delivery failure
(messages.failed_at). Without them an approach the adapter could not
deliver rendered in the lead's history exactly like one that reached
the customer — the salesperson then "followed up" on a message nobody
ever received. The inbox already shows this; the timeline must not be
the one read that hides it.

kind.description:
Kind is the message type ('text', 'image', 'audio', …). Carried so a photo
reads as a photo instead of vanishing.

text.description:
Text is what was actually said. Empty for a media-only message, which the
client renders as its Kind rather than as a blank line.

invite_sent_at.description:
InviteSentAt captures the moment an admin invited (or re-invited)
this user. Pairs with !is_email_verified to decide whether the
Team screen renders a "Pending" badge + "Resend" action.

last_seen_at.description:
LastSeenAt is stamped by the auth middleware on JWT-validated
requests (throttled to once per 5 minutes at the SQL layer).
Nullable because brand-new invited users haven't logged in yet.

picture.description: Profile picture URL (populated for Google sign-ins)

signature.description:
Signature is an optional short text the attendant can append to
MANUAL replies from the composer (US-018). Client-side insert only —
never applied to AI responses.

terms_accepted_at.description:
LGPD: when the user explicitly accepted the Terms + Privacy Policy
(NULL = never; legacy users get a v0 backfill via migration). The
version is stored so a Terms update can require fresh acceptance.

budget_cents.description:
BudgetCents is the ceiling in force (nil = none): the customer's own
or the platform default — BudgetSource says which.

budget_used_pct.description:
BudgetUsedPct is cycle spend over the ceiling, 0–100+ (may exceed
100 when the ceiling was lowered mid-cycle).

projected_monthly_brl_cents.description:
ProjectedMonthlyBRLCents extrapolates the last 30 days to a month.
Zero when there is no history — rendered as "—", never as "R$ 0 de
custo garantido".

resets_at.description: ResetsAt is when the cycle window rolls.

business_lines.description:
BusinessLines / Territory: what the company does and where. The
onboarding asks them first and reads them back from here on resume.

currency.description:
Currency is the account's immutable billing currency, set at
signup from the user's locale (US-001). The dashboard uses it to
pick the plan catalogue + price formatting (R$ vs $).

is_contract_plan.description:
IsContractPlan flags Partner / Enterprise accounts where the plan
is sold via off-platform contract (no Stripe price). The dashboard
uses this to hide self-serve checkout buttons and surface the BYOK
API-keys settings card.

openai_key_masked.description:
OpenAIKeyMasked / GeminiKeyMasked are the safe-to-display previews
of the BYOK keys (first 4 + last 4 chars). Empty string means
"not configured". Always empty for non-contract accounts so the
platform's env keys never leak into a /me response.

trial_bypass.description:
TrialBypass exempts the account from the trial/subscription gate
(owner-provisioned contract deals, Meta reviewers). The dashboard
uses it to suppress every "trial expired / upgrade" banner — such an
account is never billing-locked even if its trial window lapsed.

trial_days_remaining.description:
TrialDaysRemaining is computed from trial_expires_at so the Flutter
app can render a countdown banner without re-doing the timezone math.
Zero when the trial is over (or missing a deadline). Null when the
account has already converted to a paid plan.

checked.description:
Checked reports whether the AI half actually ran. False means only
the pattern pass happened — a clean result then means "no known
pattern", not "reviewed and approved".

safe.description:
Safe is false when anything was found. It is NOT a permission gate:
the human still decides. Blocking on a model's opinion would move
the decision away from the person who answers for the message.

kind.description:
Kind is stable and machine-readable so the UI can group and the
product can count: promise | invented_fact | out_of_scope |
placeholder | tone.

quote.description:
Quote is the offending fragment, verbatim, so the reader finds it
without re-reading the whole message.

why.description:
Why explains the consequence, not the rule. "Promete prazo" is a
label; "se o técnico atrasar, essa frase vira compromisso escrito"
is a reason someone acts on.

mfa_required.description:
MfaRequired is true when the user has 2FA enabled. The client
receives MfaSession (instead of Token) and trades it back via
/auth/2fa/verify-login with a fresh TOTP code.

skipped.description:
Skipped counts leads that were not waiting for approval (already sent,
already lost, not the caller's) — not an error, just not queue items.

drafted.description: Drafted is the number of leads moved into the approval queue.

lead_ids.description: LeadIDs are the ids successfully queued, so the UI can refresh them.

skipped_budget.description:
SkippedBudget is the number of leads the plan's monthly draft allowance
did not cover (K4). Reported rather than swallowed: a batch that
silently returns 40 of 100 reads as "only 40 were possible", and the
customer never learns there is an upgrade that would have drafted the
rest.

skipped_error.description:
SkippedError is the number of leads whose draft generation failed and
were left untouched (best-effort; the batch never aborts on one failure).

skipped_opted_out.description:
SkippedOptedOut is the number of leads skipped because the contact opted
out of receiving messages (filtered BEFORE enqueuing, per US-020 AC).

stopped_reason.description:
StoppedReason is set when the batch gave up because every draft was
failing the same way. Empty means the batch ran to the end. It is the
difference between "this lead did not work" and "nothing can work for
this account until somebody fixes X", and the screen shows it.

failed_lead_ids.description:
FailedLeadIDs are per-lead refusals (opted out, not draftable). The
rest of the batch still ran.

remaining_lead_ids.description:
RemainingLeadIDs were not attempted: past the per-call cap, or after
an account-wide stop (spend cap, empty catalogue). The client sends
them again on the next call.

stopped_reason.description:
StoppedReason is the AppError code of an account-wide refusal that
aborted the loop, empty when the batch simply hit the per-call cap.

active_accounts.description: ActiveAccounts is paying accounts (latest event not a churn).

arpa_cents.description:
ARPACents is average revenue per active account (MRR / active),
in consolidated BRL cents.

churn_rate.description: ChurnRate is churned / (active + churned) over the window, [0,1].

churned_in_window.description: ChurnedInWindow is churn events within the window.

ltv_cents.description:
LTVCents is estimated lifetime value: ARPA / churn rate. Zero when
churn rate is zero (lifetime unbounded — not meaningful to render).

mrr_brl_cents.description: MRRBRLCents is the BRL-native slice of MRR (BRL accounts only).

mrr_cents.description:
MRRCents is monthly recurring revenue consolidated in BRL cents:
the BRL slice plus the USD slice converted at USDBRLRateCents.

mrr_usd_cents.description: MRRUSDCents is the USD slice of MRR, in USD cents (unconverted).

usd_brl_rate_cents.description: USDBRLRateCents is the conversion rate applied (BRL cents per USD).

window_days.description: WindowDays is the churn lookback window used.

empty.description:
Empty says the account has no pipeline at all, so the client shows the
activation checklist instead of a wall of zeros. A brand-new account
reading "0 · 0 · 0 · R$ 0" learns that the product does nothing.

total_actions.description:
TotalActions is how many actions exist after snoozes, before the
visible-rows cut. Exposed so the screen can say "+7" instead of
implying the six shown are everything.

warnings.description:
Warnings names the sections that failed to load. A blown query
degrades to a named gap rather than an empty list that reads as
"nothing needs you".

confirmed.description:
Confirmed repeats the gate for the client: an unconfirmed reading produces
NO flags, and the screen has to say why rather than showing an empty list
that looks like a clean contract.

total_at_stake_cents.description:
TotalAtStakeCents is what the whole list is worth. The number that decides
whether somebody opens it.

scanning.description:
Scanning is true while the sweep has not covered this territory yet —
an empty calendar on day one means "still reading", not "nothing found",
and a screen that cannot tell those apart teaches people to distrust it.

states.description:
States and Keywords are what the account is watching. An empty list with
no keywords is a configuration answer, not "nothing is happening".

window_days.description: WindowDays is how far ahead this looked.

days_left.description:
DaysLeft is negative for a window that has just closed. Null never
happens here — the query only returns dated rows — but the pointer
keeps the contract honest if that ever changes.

price_registry.description:
PriceRegistry says this was bought under an ata: a twelve-month licence
to sell at a registered price, not a single closed purchase. Worth more
to a supplier than the contract itself.

rides_others.description:
RidesOthers is PNCP's `frutoAdesao` — this buyer took a ride on somebody
else's registry. The most actionable bit in the record: a buyer who
rides can buy from you without running a tender at all.

url.description:
URL is the public record, so every claim built on this can be checked
by the person who receives it.

key.description:
Key is the credential, returned at creation and never again: only its
SHA-256 hash is stored, so there is no "show me the key" to build later
even if somebody asks for one.

invite_token.description:
InviteToken is the one-shot permission from /register?invite=… (sales-led
flow, docs/fluxo-criacao-conta.md). With registration paused it is the
ONLY way in; a valid token also makes the account be born on the
invite's contracted plan instead of trial.

locale.description:
Locale is the client's DEVICE locale tag at signup (e.g. "en-US",
"pt-BR", "de-DE"). Optional — it only decides the account's
immutable billing currency (only a real en-US → USD, everything
else → BRL — US-017 review fixes).

referral_code.description:
ReferralCode is the referrer's code forwarded from a ?ref=CODE
signup link (US-174). Optional; an unknown code is silently ignored.

terms_accepted.description:
LGPD: must be true. The frontend renders the Terms + Privacy Policy
links next to the checkbox; submitting without ticking it is a 400.

utm_source.description:
First-touch acquisition attribution forwarded from the marketing
site's register CTA (utm_*). Optional; absent for social-auth and
direct signups.

token.description:
Token is the plaintext credential — returned exactly once at
creation; only the SHA-256 hash is stored.

body.description:
Body is the salesperson's own words. Optional: the rendered item block is
appended to whatever is here, so an empty body still produces a readable
offer rather than an empty message.

bought.description:
Bought is what the customer already buys, so the screen can show the
evidence next to the suggestion instead of an unexplained product name.

already_in_base.description:
AlreadyInBase names rows whose customer the account already has.
Reported rather than skipped in silence: somebody re-importing an
updated list needs to know which rows the import will not touch.

importable.description:
Counted server-side so the screen states the same numbers the import
will act on.

warnings.description:
Warnings names the sections that failed to load (best-effort reads). Empty
on a fully successful bootstrap. The client can decide whether to retry
the affected section via its dedicated endpoint.

max_leads_per_month.description:
What the customer actually buys today (US-M013). These caps already existed
on the plan and were already ENFORCED — the enrichment one blocks company
research mid-task — but never left the server. Whoever hit one found out by
clicking.

draft.description: Draft duplicates lead.approach_draft for the client's convenience.

reason.description:
Reason is set when Status is not ready: one of the FirstOfferReason*
constants.

impersonating_actor.description:
ImpersonatingActor — non-empty when the JWT was minted by the
owner panel's /impersonate endpoint. The dashboard reads this
(server-truth, not local storage) to gate the red banner.
Populated by the handler from gin context, not the use case.

is_platform_account.description:
IsPlatformAccount is true only for the Replider platform account
(PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_ID) — the app uses it to decide whether to show
the seller (vendedores) panel. Always false when unconfigured.

is_seller.description:
IsSeller is the explicit owner-granted seller flag (US-014). The
seller panel entry needs BOTH is_platform_account and is_seller —
a regular platform attendant is not a payable seller.

ai_cost_brl_cents.description:
Transparent token metering (US-M015): what the provider charged this
cycle, passed through with no markup. Nil when metering is unwired —
absent, never a zero that would read as "AI was free this month".

overage_conversations_count.description:
Conversation overage (see docs/OVERAGE_METERING_DESIGN.md). Lets
the dashboard tell the user it has passed the plan franchise and
is now paying per conversation, and how much so far this cycle.

leads_created.description:
LeadsCreated is how many of the created customers landed in the
default funnel (see SetLeadMaker). Zero when the maker is unwired.

skipped.description: Skipped counts rows that arrived unimportable or already existed.

Skipped counts rows that arrived unimportable or were already identical.
Reported so a count that does not match the selection has an explanation.

updated.description:
Updated counts rows whose product already existed under the same name
and got the file's price (and description, when it carried one). A
re-imported price list is a list of new prices, and skipping them was
the whole reason the catalogue drifted from the spreadsheet.

skipped.description:
Skipped counts selections that were already imported or that name an
address this account never discovered — reported rather than silently
ignored, because a count that does not match the selection is a question.
Skipped counts rows that arrived unimportable or already recorded.

competencia.description:
Competencia ("2026-07") is the DATASUS month the counts come from —
the card says "dados CNES de 07/2026", never "hoje".

matched_by.description:
MatchedBy says how the bridge landed ("phone" | "name") so the UI can
qualify the claim honestly.

matches.description:
Matches are the account's OWN products that fit this park.

The answer to "what can I offer this hospital", available before
spending anything: the crossing is a string match between the
catalogue's words and the equipment the registry lists, so it needs no
model at all. The AI was only ever needed to WRITE the message; picking
what fits is arithmetic, and hiding it behind a paid call meant nobody
could see the opportunity without first paying for a draft.

truncated.description:
Truncated says the cap cut the history. Reported rather than implied: a
list that silently starts mid-conversation reads as "this is everything",
and the first line then looks like the beginning of the relationship.

week_start.description: WeekStart is Monday 00:00 in the account's timezone.

progress.description:
Progress is how far along, for a bar that means something: the ladder has
a known length, so this is a fact rather than an estimate.

suggestions.description: Suggestions are the audience chips, only on that step.

hidden_targets.description:
HiddenTargets is the teaser: how many named targets the report is NOT
showing. The line the pitch is built on.

total_establishments.description:
TotalEstablishments counts DISTINCT establishments holding any of the
asked equipment (not the per-category sum — one hospital with two
categories is one door to knock on).

equipment.description:
Equipment is the registry's own label for what they have, and QtExist
how many they declare — a count, never an age.

already_lead.description:
AlreadyLead is true when this business is already in the funnel.
SHOWN rather than filtered: a list that silently drops half its
results looks like a weak source, when the real news is that the
search is repeating work already done.

external_id.description:
ExternalID is the dedup key — the E.164 phone when there is one, the
place id otherwise. Round-trips to the import so the second call does
not have to search again.

handoff.description:
Handoff is true when the agent decided to pass the conversation to
a person. In a real conversation the pipeline reacts by pausing the
bot; in the preview there is nobody to hand off TO, so the flag
exists to let the client explain what would have happened instead of
rendering the control token.

suggestions.description:
Suggestions carries 3 polite follow-up questions generated by
the AI at the end of each turn. The frontend renders them as
clickable chips; tapping one pre-fills the input and the next
turn gets new context-aware suggestions. Empty when the model
didn't produce the expected [SUGESTOES] block (fallback to the
template's static set happens client-side).

already_in_catalogue.description:
AlreadyInCatalogue names rows whose product already exists. Reported rather
than skipped silently: somebody re-importing an updated price list needs to
know the old row is the one that stays.

importable.description:
Importable and Problems are counted server-side so the screen states the
same numbers the import will act on.

new_count.description:
NewCount excludes the duplicates: the number the button should offer
to import.

remaining_this_month.description:
RemainingThisMonth is the lead allowance left, or nil when the plan
does not meter leads. The cost of a decision belongs next to the
decision — finding out afterwards that a search ate the month is how
somebody stops trusting the feature.

would_import.description:
WouldImport is what the button will actually create: the smaller of
the selection and what the allowance permits.

disabled.description: true when we just disabled the row (Gone)

cnes.description:
CNES identifies a park item's establishment for a future
draft-from-park call.

competencia.description:
Competencia ("2026-07") is the DATASUS month a park item's counts
come from — in September the data is July (45–75 day lag), and the
card says so instead of implying "today".

id.description:
ID is stable per underlying fact (signal id, CNES id, contact id,
date id) so the client can key rows and a refresh does not reshuffle
identity.

lead_id.description:
LeadID links to the queue draft the auto-offer already created
(licitação) — the CTA is then "open the draft", not "prepare".

matches.description:
Matches is what of the catalogue fits what THIS establishment
declares — the same crossing the lead panel does, brought forward to
the radar so the seller sees the offer before opening anything.

value_cents.description:
ValueCents is the money attached, when the source publishes one.
Zero = not disclosed, never "zero reais".

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_us.description:
Park is how big the park opportunity actually is, beyond the page of
items above. Nil when the account has no territory or no catalogue
word that resolves to CNES equipment.

equipment.description:
Equipment names what the catalogue matched in the CNES dictionary,
so the number above is auditable instead of a bare claim.

warnings.description:
Warnings names the collectors that failed — an empty feed is a claim,
and a query that blew up has not earned it.

github_com_replider_api_internal_core_us.description:
The month's consumption in the units the customer buys. Tokens are our
cost; what they purchase is leads, research and approaches. Absent when it
cannot be counted — a zero here would read as "I used nothing", which is
different from "I don't know".

business_minutes.description:
BusinessMinutes the first human response took (or has been
pending, when unanswered) inside the business window.

already_recorded.description: AlreadyRecorded names rows whose sale the account already has.

importable.description:
Counted server-side so the screen states the numbers the import will
act on.

unknown_customers.description:
UnknownCustomers names rows whose customer is not in the base — the
number that tells the person to import the customer list first.

contact_id.description:
ContactID / ContactName are the resolution: who in the base this row
is. Empty with a Problem when nobody matched.

customer.description:
Customer is the cell as typed: an e-mail, a phone or a name. Which of
the three it is gets decided at resolution time, not here.

date.description:
Date is the cell as typed; SoldAt is what it parsed to (zero when it
did not). Both travel so the preview can show the person the text they
wrote next to the date the import will use.

duplicate.description:
Duplicate marks "already recorded" structurally, so the client renders
it as the fact it is rather than with the error icon.

line.description: Line is the 1-based line in the original file, header included.

problem.description: Problem is empty when the row may create a sale.

product.description:
Product is the cell as typed. Matched against the catalogue by name;
when nothing matches it becomes the item's free description.

product_id.description: ProductID is set when Product matched the catalogue.

complete.description:
Complete reports whether the walk reached the bottom of the folder. False
means the cap stopped it, which the UI says out loud rather than implying
the list is everybody.

mailbox.description:
Mailbox is the folder that was read, echoed so a customer whose Sent
folder has an unusual name can see we found the right one.

scanned.description:
Scanned is how many messages were read; Found is how many DISTINCT
addresses came out of them. Both, because "read 4000, found 60" is the
sentence that explains why the list is short.

skipped.description: Skipped counts addresses left out as automated or as the account's own.

commission_currency.description:
CommissionCurrency: the currency every profit/commission figure is
in (always BRL by ledger construction — MRR is the only per-account
currency field). The app formats from this, never a hardcode.

last_closed_cycle.description:
LastClosedCycle (YYYY-MM) is the month before the current one —
the newest cycle the recompute can have fully settled.

action.description:
Action is the ladder step that streak maps to:
none/warning/reduced/flag_reallocation.

breach.description:
Breach: the cycle's breached % currently exceeds the configured
cut (strict >, same rule as the compute).

consecutive_breaches.description:
ConsecutiveBreaches the current cycle would close with (previous
cycle's persisted streak + this one).

previous_cycle_action.description:
PreviousCycleAction is the last SETTLED ladder step (previous
cycle's persisted state; "none" when never computed).

within_sla_pct.description:
WithinSLAPct = 100 × (total − breached) / total; 100 with no
conversations yet.

commission_currency.description:
CommissionCurrency: currency of every amount/breakdown figure
(always BRL by ledger construction) — the app formats from this.

cycle.description: Cycle being shown (YYYY-MM); defaults to the last closed one.

cycles.description:
Cycles the selector offers: every cycle with ledger entries plus
the current (open) and last closed ones, newest first.

is_open.description:
IsOpen: the cycle hasn't closed yet (current or future month) —
every number is a partial preview ("prévia"), not a settled
statement.

pix_key.description: PixKey is the seller's payout key (nil = not set yet).

locale.description:
Locale is the client's DEVICE locale tag (e.g. "en-US", "pt-BR"),
used only when this social login creates a brand-new account —
it decides the immutable billing currency (only a real en-US →
USD, US-017 review fixes). Ignored on login to an existing account.

referral_code.description:
ReferralCode is the ?ref=CODE captured from the signup link,
forwarded so social signups get the same seller attribution
(US-003) as email/password ones. Only consulted when this login
creates a brand-new account; unknown codes silently ignored.

is_new.description: true if this is a new user created via social login

already_known.description:
AlreadyKnown marks a hit that is already in this account's contacts
via a previous park offer.

total.description:
Total is how many units of the asked equipment the establishment
declares to CNES. A count, never an age.

cities.description:
Cities lists the territory cities the hunt was narrowed to; empty
means the whole UF (no cities in the territory, or none resolved).

competencia.description: Competencia ("2026-07") is the DATASUS month the counts come from.

note.description:
Note explains an empty answer (no dictionary match, or the UF's data
not ingested yet) — an empty list with no reason reads as "nobody has
it", which is a claim the data has not earned.

business_lines.description:
BusinessLines: nil means "don't touch"; an empty list clears them.
Each entry must be one of sell / rent / service.

weekly_digest_opt_out.description:
WeeklyDigestOptOut toggles the per-account weekly retention digest
(US-176). true = stop sending; false = resume. nil = don't touch.

signature.description:
Signature is the attendant's optional manual-reply sign-off (US-018).
The composer offers it on manual sends; never applied to AI replies.

totp_enabled.description:
TOTPEnabled lets the dashboard render the 2FA card state instantly
from the cached /me user instead of waiting on a dedicated
GET /me/2fa/status round-trip.

template_id.description:
Mission 7: optional. When both template_id and placeholders
are supplied, the server applies placeholders to the template
prompt (caller's system_prompt wins if set) and seeds a
"Perguntas frequentes" knowledge source with the template's
Q/A pairs.

registration_enabled.description:
RegistrationEnabled mirrors REGISTRATION_ENABLED. When false the
register screen hides its form and shows an "em breve" state; the
API refuses the signup anyway (REGISTRATION_PAUSED, 503) — this is
only so the client never offers a door that is closed.

media_url.description: GCS object_path from /media/upload, or external URL

subject.description: Subject is honoured on EMAIL conversations only.

business_hours_start.description:
Nilable so that omitting the fields means "don't touch". Days=0
explicitly disables the business-hours window (24/7 bot).

object_path.description: store this as media_url when calling /reply

signed_url.description: V4 signed PUT URL; expires in 15 min

contract_title.description:
ContractTitle is filled on read, so a list of alerts is readable without a
second fetch per row.

days_until_due.description:
DaysUntilDue is NEGATIVE once the deadline passed — the state that costs
money, which must not read as zero.

lead_id.description: LeadID is the renewal lead this alert produced, when it produced one.

anticipated_objections.description:
AnticipatedObjections is what the matcher call expects THIS customer
to push back with, already answered: [{label, counter}]. Shown on the
approval card and injected into the draft so the text can preempt it.

board_pos.description:
BoardPos is the manually chosen rank inside the column (fractional
ranking, see ComputeBoardPos). Nil = never manually placed: the card
keeps the automatic most-stalled-first order, AFTER every placed one.
Written only by a drag (FunnelStageRepository.MoveLead) and cleared by
the column's reset-order action.

contact_address.description:
ContactAddress is the same kind of display-only join, but always the
ADDRESS the message would go to — never the name. The approval step
needs it: a name cannot catch a wrong number.

contact_label.description:
ContactLabel is a DISPLAY-ONLY join (never persisted): the human name,
phone or email behind ContactID. Every outbound approval shows the
operator who the message will reach, and a ULID answers that question
with nothing.

matched_products.description:
MatchedProducts is which of the account's products this lead's offer
is about, and why: [{product_id, name, reason}]. Chosen by the offer
matcher against the catalogue; the draft, the card and the approval
screen read the same pick. Empty until drafted.

owner_user_id.description:
OwnerUserID is the salesperson responsible for this lead (US-F009).
Empty/nil = unassigned, which stays visible to the whole team — a
freshly prospected lead belongs to nobody yet.

scheduled_for.description:
ScheduledFor labels an approved-but-capped card ("sai amanhã às 08h")
instead of hiding it — the send is planned, and planned work the
operator cannot see is work they will redo.

send_blocked_reason.description:
SendBlockedReason names what stops THIS card going out, when the queue
as a whole is fine. Today the only value is NO_ADDRESS.

stage_id.description:
StageID is the Kanban column the card sits in (US-M008). Nil for
leads created before the board existed, or by paths that know nothing
about it (inbound, prospecting) — those resolve onto the column
