matching their canonical status.

by_funnel.description:
ByFunnel is empty when the count failed — the list still came back, so
the screen degrades to no chips rather than to no queue.

send_blocked_reason.description:
SendBlockedReason names what stops these drafts going out, or is
absent. The screen disables the send controls and says so, instead of
offering a button that fails after the click.

total.description: Total is every draft awaiting the caller, ignoring funnel_id and paging.

email_template_id.description:
EmailTemplateID/Version attribute the send to a stored template so the
reply it earns lands on the right numbers. Optional — a text written
from scratch has no template.

template_name.description:
TemplateName is the approved WhatsApp template the approach is sent
through. Cold first-contact on WhatsApp is only deliverable via a
template (US-020) — but that rule is WhatsApp's, so it is enforced by
the use case AFTER the channel is known, not by a binding tag here.
A binding:"required" made every EMAIL approval fail at the door.

text.description:
Text is the FINAL, human-reviewed/edited message — delivered as the
approved template's BODY parameter.

via_bulk.description:
ViaBulk routes the send through the platform's bulk provider (hybrid
model): batch approvals set it, one-by-one approvals never do. Refused
with BULK_SENDING_NOT_READY unless the domain is bulk-verified.

owner_user_id.description:
A null/absent OwnerUserID UNASSIGNS. It is the only way to take a lead
from somebody without inventing a new verb.

created.description:
Created is how many became leads. Lower than Found once the cap bites,
and the difference is not a failure — it is tomorrow's batch.

found.description: Found is how many untouched establishments the territory offered.

daily_cap.description:
DailyCap bounds a bad day. Even a perfect model with a wrong prompt is
only allowed to be wrong this many times before a human has to look.

eligible_to_offer.description:
EligibleToOffer is why the dashboard shows the invitation. Computed
here so the client cannot disagree with the server about who earned it.

enabled_at.description: EnabledAt / EnabledBy is who turned it on, for the day somebody asks.

min_score.description:
MinScore is the lead quality floor. Cold outbound to a badly-matched
lead is what burns a domain, and it is the case a tired human catches
and an eager one does not.

offered_at.description:
OfferedAt records when we last asked. Nil means never — the offer is
made once and not nagged.

sent_today.description: SentToday is the cap in the operator's terms.

streak_needed.description:
StreakNeeded lets the UI say "faltam 6" instead of "not eligible",
which is the difference between a goal and a wall.

unedited_streak.description:
UneditedStreak counts consecutive approvals sent EXACTLY as drafted.
Reset by any edit or discard: the streak is evidence that the model
writes what this person would have written, and an edit is that
evidence expiring.

owner_user_id.description:
Null UNASSIGNS the whole batch — the way to undo a wrong redistribution
without clicking 200 times.

enabled.description: Enabled: the domain is registered with the provider.

ready.description: Ready: registered AND verified — batch approvals will go through.

records.description: Records the customer must publish; empty once verified.

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents is what this deal would pay the CALLER. Null when no rule
covers it: zero would read as "you earn nothing on this", which is a
different and much worse claim.

owner_user_id.description:
OwnerUserID assigns the created leads to a specific salesperson. Omitted
means unassigned, which stays visible to the whole team — NOT the caller,
because an admin importing the company's base is not claiming it.

expires_in.description:
ExpiresIn is seconds. Told to the client so a UI can say the link is
temporary instead of letting somebody paste an expiring URL into a chat.

ai_proposal.description:
AIProposal is the model's reading, verbatim. Never written by a human and
never used to drive an alert on its own.

amendments.description: Amendments is filled on a detail read: the chain in force, oldest first.

auto_renewal.description:
AutoRenewal + NoticeDays is the most expensive pair of facts in the
document: miss the window and the contract renews itself.

confirmed.description:
Confirmed says a human validated the reading. Everything downstream (G5's
alerts, G6's renewal leads) keys on this, so the client shows it too.

days_until_end.description:
DaysUntilEnd is negative once the contract has expired, which is the state
that costs money and must not read as zero.

last_adjusted_on.description:
LastAdjustedOn is when the price was actually raised. Without it an
accumulation would run from the contract's start forever and double-count
every adjustment already applied.

notice_deadline.description: NoticeDeadline is the last day to give notice before it renews itself.

object_path.description:
ObjectPath is the PDF in the private bucket. Empty when the contract was
registered from pasted text.

parent_contract_id.description:
ParentContractID chains an amendment (aditivo) to the contract it
changes; Version is its place in that chain.

price_registry.description:
The price registry (ata de registro de preços). A public body committed to
buy, the supplier delivered part of it, and the remaining balance expires
with the ata — pre-approved revenue nobody goes back for.

redacted.description:
Redacted says fields were REMOVED for the caller's role. Without this
flag a redacted value_cents of 0 reads as "this contract is free", which
is a worse lie than showing nothing — the client renders "oculto" only
because the server admitted it hid something.

registry_balance_on.description:
RegistryBalanceOn is when the balance was last known. A balance with no
date is a number nobody can trust: "R$80k left as of last week" and
"R$80k left as of a year ago" are different facts.

starts_on.description:
StartsOn/EndsOn are calendar dates: a contract runs on days, and putting
a timezone on "vence em 31/12" only creates off-by-one arguments.

recipients.description:
One of these must be provided. If both are set, RecipientsWithVars
wins (simple Recipients is ignored).

name.description:
Name is the person; Company the establishment. Phone OR Email is
required (a lead needs a way to be reached); the rest is optional.

addresses.description: Addresses is the human's selection. Required — there is no "all".

funnel_id.description:
FunnelID is where imported customers land. Required on import: a lead
with no funnel is a row nobody sees.

snooze_hours.description:
SnoozeHours is optional; omitted uses the default and anything past the
cap is clamped, because a "snooze" long enough to outlive the deadline
is a deletion with better manners.

overdue.description: Overdue is how many already lapsed, so the UI can lead with them.

total_at_stake_cents.description:
TotalAtStakeCents is what the whole list is worth. The number that decides
whether anybody opens it.

allow_open_cycle.description:
AllowOpenCycle is the explicit override to settle the RUNNING
cycle (partial payout) — without it, an open/future cycle is
rejected with COMMISSION_CYCLE_OPEN (US-005).

cycle.description:
Cycle is "YYYY-MM"; pending entries of EARLIER cycles
(adjustments) settle together.

note.description:
Note is the optional PIX transaction reference stamped on every
settled entry.

before_lead_id.description:
The drop slot's neighbors as the client rendered them: before = the
card that will sit ABOVE, after = the one BELOW. Either may be absent
at an edge; with neither, the card keeps no manual position (automatic
order). A never-placed neighbor counts as absent server-side.

pending_cents.description:
PendingCents is what this salesperson has earned in the month so far and
has not been paid yet — the tile on their own home screen.

is_default.description:
IsDefault says the account never saved its own library and these are
the vertical seed — the screen shows "padrão do setor, edite à
vontade" instead of pretending the user wrote them.

days_since_contact.description:
DaysSinceContact is the relationship's pulse. Nil when nobody ever
spoke to them, which is different from "spoke long ago".

days_until_due.description:
DaysUntilDue is the countdown. NEGATIVE when overdue, and deliberately
not clamped: "acabou há 12 dias" is the most actionable thing on the
screen, and zero would hide it.

gross_cents.description:
GrossCents and NetCents are lifetime. Net leads in the UI, because
what a customer is worth is what the company kept.

last_contact_at.description:
LastContactAt is the last message either way. The relationship's
pulse: a customer nobody has spoken to in four months is a customer a
competitor is speaking to.

next_due_at.description:
NextDueAt is when they are predicted to need it again. Nil when no
sale carried a cycle — a guessed date puts a real customer on a
follow-up list on a day nobody chose.

purchases.description:
Purchases is how many times they have bought. A repeat customer and a
one-off look identical on revenue alone.

DaysSinceContact is the relationship's pulse. Nil when nobody ever
spoke to them, which is different from "spoke long ago".

infra_cost_cents.description:
InfraCostCents is the flat infra cost per account per month in
BRL cents.

tax_bps.description: TaxBps is the tax on revenue in basis points (600 = 6%).

rendered.description:
Rendered is exactly what the approval queue will show. Sent so the review
screen never has to reproduce the server's formatting and disagree with it.

account_id.description:
AccountID narrows the recompute to one account; empty recomputes
every seller-linked account.

by_kind.description:
ByKind splits the total, because "recuperei R$400k" lands differently when
it is R$300k of forgotten index and R$100k of renewals saved.

recoveries.description:
Recoveries is the list behind the total: a headline nobody can drill into
is a headline nobody believes.

reason.description:
Reason is the reporter's own words, and optional. It is the
highest-value thing in the report — "esse fornecedor nunca manda boleto
por email" is knowledge no technical check has — but demanding it would
cost reports from people in a hurry, and a report with no reason still
protects the network.

confirmed_by_user_id.description:
ConfirmedByUserID is who approved an AI-extracted sale. Empty on a
manual one, where the person entering it IS the confirmation.

contact_id.description:
ContactID is who bought. Required: a sale with no customer cannot
feed a portfolio, which is half the reason this table exists.

cost_cents.description:
CostCents is what the goods or delivery cost. Zero is a legitimate
value for a service with no marginal cost — and a dangerous default
for a distributor, which is why the UI asks rather than assumes.

cycle_days.description:
CycleDays is how long until this customer is likely to need it again.
The single field the repurchase engine (F3) runs on — "200 caixas de
luvas, ciclo ~30d" is a prediction somebody can act on, and a sale
with no cycle is one the engine will never resurface.

gross_cents.description:
The three amounts, in cents, in Currency. Integers throughout: money
in floats accumulates error, and a cent lost per sale is an argument
with a salesperson every month.

lead_id.description:
LeadID links the deal it came from, when there was one. Optional —
plenty of sales come from a phone call nobody logged.

margin_rate.description: MarginRate is nil when nothing was sold: zero over zero is unknown.

net_cents.description:
NetCents is what the company kept: gross minus cost minus tax. THIS is
what a commission should be calculated on — a percentage of gross can
quietly exceed the whole margin.

next_purchase_due.description:
NextPurchaseDue is when this customer is likely to need it again. Nil
without a cycle: a guess would put a real customer on a follow-up list
on a date nobody chose.

seller_user_id.description:
SellerUserID is who gets the commission. Optional: a house account
sale has no salesperson, and inventing one would pay somebody for
work they did not do.

tax_cents.description:
TaxCents is what leaves for the government. Separate from cost
because a Brazilian company's tax burden is not a cost of goods and
is not negotiable the same way.

underwater.description:
Underwater flags a sale that cost more than it brought in. Surfaced,
never refused — discounts, loss leaders and typos all look like this,
and only a person can tell which.

text.description:
Text is what the person wrote. Empty is allowed and meaningful: clearing
the box is an edit, and refusing to persist it would resurrect a draft
they deliberately deleted.

payload.description:
Payload is the full domain.Message shape — Type/Content/MediaURL
/Metadata. Stored opaque so adding new types later doesn't need
a schema change here.

business_hours_only.description:
BusinessHoursOnly holds sends until the next working hour. A cold
email at 03:14 reads as a machine, which is exactly what it must not.

step_stats.description:
Steps is the funnel: how many reached each step and how many replied
after it. Named separately from Sequence.Steps, which is the plan.

stop_on_reply.description:
StopOnReply defaults TRUE and there is deliberately no UI to turn it
off. It is exposed as a field only so the rule is visible in the
payload the editor renders at the top of the screen.

bonus_nps_cents.description:
BonusNPSCents is the fixed promoter-NPS bonus (US-008), integer
BRL cents; 0 disables it.

bonus_retention_cents.description:
BonusRetentionCents is the one-time 12-active-months bonus,
integer BRL cents; 0 disables it.

breach_pct.description:
BreachPct: the cycle breaches when MORE than this % of the
seller's assigned conversations blow the threshold.

business_start_hour.description:
Business window hours [start, end) in Timezone; weekends are
always excluded.

first_response_minutes.description:
FirstResponseMinutes is the SLA threshold in business minutes
(default 240 = 4 business hours).

closes_at.description: ClosesAt is the deadline. After it the signal is dead — see Expired.

cnpj.description:
CNPJ, when the source gives one — the join key to everything else we
know about this company.

days_left.description:
DaysLeft is nil when the source published no deadline. Three days is a
reason to write today; thirty is a reason to prepare properly, and the
difference is the whole value of the signal.

dismissed_at.description:
DismissedAt records a human saying "not for us". Kept rather than
deleted so the same tender does not come back tomorrow.

external_id.description:
ExternalID is the source's own identifier, and the dedup key. PNCP
republishes the same tender as it is amended, and a salesperson who
gets the same "novo edital" three times stops reading them.

lead_id.description:
LeadID is set once somebody acts on this signal, so the same tender
is not worked twice by two people.

organization.description: Organization is who published it, as a human recognises them.

url.description:
URL is the source page, so the salesperson can read the actual notice
rather than trusting our summary of it.

value_cents.description:
ValueCents is the estimated amount, when published. Zero means "not
disclosed", which is common and is NOT the same as zero reais.

signed_at.description:
SignedAt and SaleID are what make the card say "assinado e venda
registrada" rather than just "assinado".

callback_url.description:
CallbackURL is what the customer pastes into their provider's webhook
settings. Built here because the client does not know the API's own origin.

has_token.description:
HasToken tells a screen whether the integration is configured without
handing the token back.

webhook_token.description: WebhookToken is the unguessable part of OUR inbound URL.

reachable.description:
Reachable is false when the last poll could not read the source at
all. The screen says so instead of presenting stored tenders as today's.

statements.description:
Statements is one per salesperson, most owed first — the order an admin
reviews in.

total_pending_cents.description: TotalPendingCents is what closing the whole month would cost.

arguments.description:
Arguments are what to lead with. Ordered by the author, because the
order IS the argument.

author_user_id.description:
AuthorUserID is recognition, and recognition is what makes a
salesperson contribute one. A strategy with no visible author is a
company document; one with a name on it is somebody's method.

channel_mix.description:
ChannelMix is the plan: which channels in which order. Free text
rather than a structured cadence, because a strategy describes an
intent and a Sequence implements it — conflating them would make
every wording change a migration.

icp.description: ICP is who this is for, in the seller's own words.

objections.description:
Objections map what they say to what to answer. The part of a
strategy that a new salesperson actually reads.

sequence_id.description:
SequenceID links the cadence that implements this strategy, when one
exists. Optional: a strategy is worth writing down before anyone has
built the automation for it.

stats.description:
Stats is per VERSION: an approach sent under version 2 must not count
toward version 3's numbers, which is the whole reason versions exist.

triggers.description:
Triggers are the moments this strategy applies: "publicou edital",
"trocou de diretor clínico".

version.description:
Version is bumped when the CONTENT changes. "Essa estratégia converte
14%" is meaningless if the arguments were rewritten twice since the
number was earned — the same reason email templates version.

channel_id.description:
ChannelID scopes channel-level suggestions (whatsapp_ban_risk is
dismissed per channel, US-022). Ignored for account-level types.

funnel_id.description:
Scope follows the brand-kit cascade: global, one funnel, or one
salesperson. Both nil means the whole company.

too_long.description:
TooLong flags a body past the point where a cold email stops being
read. A warning, not a limit — the person writing knows their market.

Version is bumped on every save, because "this template gets 12% reply"
is meaningless if the text changed twice since the number was earned.
